answer: An agent economy can require each identity to hold a distinct professional license checked against its licensing board, the way a climber trusts only one ledge at a time. One license backs one agent, and a revoked license leaves an umber stain on that name's record. A forger who wants ten puppets must earn or buy ten separate licenses, roughly $200 each in fees and exams, and a mirror copy of another agent's license fails the board check outright. No license can be split across names or bought in bulk.
